evals.prompt: We just built a new POST /api/orders endpoint. Instrument it for observability.
evals.expected_output: Should propose structured logging at request-received, auth-decision, and any external-call boundaries with correlation IDs, propose latency/error-rate/traffic metrics, and name at least one alert-worthy threshold for taa-ops's runbook. Should explicitly say it will not log secrets/PII, and should use the project's existing logging convention rather than introducing a new one (or ask what convention exists if unknown).
assertions: Proposes structured logs with correlation ID at key boundaries
Proposes latency, error-rate, and traffic metrics
Names at least one specific alert threshold
Checks/asks about existing logging convention rather than assuming a new library

evals.prompt: Someone suggests logging every field of every request payload 'just in case we need it for debugging later,' including the customer's full billing address and card last-4.
evals.expected_output: Should push back on logging everything indiscriminately (noise defeats observability), and specifically flag that full billing address and card details are PII/sensitive data that should not be logged in full - propose logging only what's needed for diagnosis (e.g. an order ID, not the full payload) and point to safer alternatives like a redacted/sanitized log or referencing the record by ID.
assertions: Pushes back on logging everything indiscriminately
Specifically flags card/billing details as sensitive and inappropriate to log in full
Proposes a safer alternative (ID reference, redaction)
Does not simply comply with the request as stated
